conflicts.fact: Which organelles animal cells have or lack (vacuole, centrioles, lysosomes), and which organelles are 'shared'
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says animal cells lack a large central vacuole and have centrioles and lysosomes (plant cells lack them). Lesson 4 lists shared organelles as nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes, membrane, rough ER, Golgi but omits lysosomes. Lesson 5 treats lysosomes as one of the 10 organelles on the plant cell master diagram, so lysosomes are in the plant cell there but plant-absent in Lesson 3.

conflicts.fact: Lesson 3 Model phase says animal cell is the second layer added to the plant cell model, whereas Lesson 4 says the cumulative model is the animal cell from Lesson 3 and the plant cell is added alongside
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3: learners add a human cheek cell to the earlier plant cell sketch from Lesson 1 and Lesson 2 (plant first, animal added second). Lesson 4: the cumulative model is the animal cell built in Lesson 3, and the plant cell is drawn as the new second diagram. Lesson 5: the plant cell model was started in Lesson 4.

conflicts.fact: Whether the sukuma wiki electron micrograph was studied in Lesson 2 and what Lesson 3 says about it
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 says learners 'study the same sukuma wiki plant cell electron micrograph from Lesson 2' and says the light microscope was used in Lesson 1 only, and Lesson 4 says the plant cell EM/organelles were first examined in detail only then. Lesson 2 uses fact-sheet images, with Lesson 1 projecting the EM, so which lesson introduced the EM image differs.

conflicts.fact: Which lesson the cumulative model was started in
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: Anchor Model Version 1 drawn in Lesson 1 and updated every lesson. Lesson 2: model 'begun in Lesson 1 or started fresh if this is the first opportunity'. Lesson 6 Teacher says 'Open your cumulative journal model from Lesson 2', while its learner text says since Lesson 1.

conflicts.fact: Light microscope magnification/specimen in Lesson 1 vs Lesson 2 images
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1: learners prepare a wet mount of hand-cut leaf section (or peeled epidermis) and see compartments with green granules. Lesson 2 Image A is described as a 'cross-section' photomicrograph at the school; Lesson 6 uses 400× mesophyll tissue. Light-microscope resolution is stated as ~200 nm in Lesson 2 while Lesson 1 gives a 4×–40× objective range, with a 400× photomicrograph, an inconsistent magnification description.

conflicts.fact: What the large fluid-filled space is called and the Lesson 2 claim that the electron microscope reveals 'nanometre-scale' structures
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says the large fluid-filled space and organelles are revealed purely due to the electron microscope's resolution (~0.1–0.2 nm vs ~200 nm), while Lesson 4 and others identify the vacuole and chloroplasts as structures that are visible in a light microscope (chloroplasts are the green granules seen in Lesson 1). Lesson 2 calls them invisible under the school light microscope.

conflicts.fact: Which organelle material is used for the nucleus/mitochondria and the Lesson reference for animal cell images
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says learners revisit electron micrographs from Lessons 3 and 4 and describes the animal cell as used in Lesson 3 and the sukuma wiki cell in Lesson 4, but Lesson 7's Observed says the sukuma wiki EM was the puzzle from the original phenomenon (Lesson 1/2). Lesson 3 says the sukuma wiki EM was from Lesson 2.
